member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfEntity
member.summary: Base class for AutoCAD entities (graphical objects like lines, circles etc).

remarks.para: The main properties of an entity are , , , and .

An entity is either in model space or in paper space (see property ). By default an entity is in model space. A model space entity must be part of DxfModel.Entities, a paper space entity must be part of DxfLayout.Entities of the paper space layout on which the entity is shown. The exception to this rule is when the entity is part of a , which can be shown on either model or paper space, depending on if the referencing is in model or paper space. When showing model space (see DxfHeader.ShowModelSpace), entities in paper space are invisible. When showing paper space, entities in model space are first transformed to paper space as specified by a view port. Entities in paper space are not transformed.

member.name: M:WW.Cad.Model.IPathDrawer.IsSeparateCharDrawingPreferred
member.summary: Is this drawer gaining from drawing separate chars rather than drawing complete strings?
member.remarks: Usually a complete string is draw as one path. Splitting this into single paths for each letter is an order N algorithm (N being the number of letters), so if the drawer works with less effiency depending on the number of paths/points involved (N log N or worse) it should return true here. But be sure to test both cases with a TTF text intensive file because sometimes the memory overhead of creating all new paths eat up the gain.
member.returns: true if this drawer gains from small filled paths, false otherwise

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.DxfValueFormat.DecimalNumber.Precision
member.summary: Gets or sets the precision.

remarks.para: For decimal, engineering and scientific units the precision indicates the number of decimals.

For architectural units the precision corresponds to the precision in inches:
value precision in feet/inches
0 0'0"
1 0'0 1/2"
1 0'0 1/4"
1 0'0 1/8"
1 0'0 1/16"
1 0'0 1/32"
1 0'0 1/64"
1 0'0 1/128"
1 0'0 1/256"

For fractional units the precision corresponds to the denominator:
value denominator
0 0
1 0 1/2
1 0 1/4
1 0 1/8
1 0 1/16
1 0 1/32
1 0 1/64
1 0 1/128
1 0 1/256

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.DxfValueFormat.Date.FormatString
member.summary: Gets or sets the format string (the default value is null).
member.remarks:
The following sub strings can be used in the date format string.
Sub string Explanation
M month number
d day number
dd day number
yy year number (2 digits)
yyyy year number (4 digits)
dddd day spelled out
MMMM month spelled out
MMM 3 letter abbreviation of month
h hours (0-11)
HH hours (0-23)
mm minutes
ss seconds
tt AM/PM
%#x regional long date: e.g. Saturday, March 29, 2008
%#c regional long date time: e.g. Saturday, March 29, 2008 7:51:24 PM
%x regional short date: e.g. 3/29/2008
%c regional short date time: e.g. 3/29/2008 7:51:24 PM
%X regional time

member.name: M:WW.Cad.Base.DxfUtil.DisposeThreadStaticObjects
member.summary: Dispose all thread static objects.

remarks.para: Normally all thread static objects are released by the garbage collector when a thread ends, but method Dipose is not called on objects. With this method these disposable objects can be explicitly disposed of at the end of a thread.

An MLine references an object defining the number, spacing, and appearance of the parallel lines.

This entity was introduced in release 13.
Unlike most entities, the z-axis does not affect the rendering of the MLine.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfMLine.Segment.Element.Parameters
member.summary: Gets the element parameters.
member.remarks: The list may contain zero or more items. The first value is the distance from the segment vertex along the miter line to the point where the line element's path intersects the miter line. The next value is the distance along the line element's path from the point defined by the value to the actual start of the line element. The next is the distance from the start of the line element to the first break (or cut) in the line element. The successive values continue to list the start and stop points of the line element in this segment of the mline. Linetypes do not affect these value.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfMLine.Segment.Element.AreaFillParameters
member.summary: Gets the area fill parameters.
member.remarks:
Similar to , it describes the parameterization of the fill area for this mline segment. The values are interpreted identically to the
and when taken as a whole for all line elements in the mline segment, they define the boundary of the fill area for the mline segment.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfRasterImage.BoundaryVertices
member.summary: Gets the boundary vertices of the visible portion of the image.

remarks.para: The boundary vertices are defined in image coordinates, the origin being the center of the top left pixel of the image. The x-axis points right and the y-axis points down. Use 2 boundary vertices to indicate the opposite corners of a rectangle boundary. Use more vertices to create a polygonal boundary.
This property must be set, otherwise the image is not visible. Use method to set the default boundary vertices that shows the entire image.
However polygonal boundaries can specified, CadLib currently only renders rectangular images.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.BasicEntityVisitor
member.summary: Basic do-nothing implementation of an entity visitor.

remarks.para: It is useful as a base class for writing your own entity visitor in case you are only interested in special entities.

Please be aware that entities are organized in a tree, so in order to walk the complete tree you'll need to get throw the entity walker to the sub entities of DxfDimension, DxfInsert, DxfTable, and DxfPolyline.

Extending from this class has the further impact that new entity types added to CadLib will not break your code because in this case this class will be adopted. This may be an advantage or disadvantage depending on the purpose of your class. As a rule of thumb extend this class if you are only interested in some special entity types, and extend the basic interface if you want to reach all entities.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.CloneContext
member.summary: Represents a clone context that facilitates making clones of object graphs.

remarks.para: The clone context enables making a clone of multiple objects and fixing the object references after all objects are cloned. To resolve these references, call method after all objects have been cloned. E.g. e hatch entity may reference a circle entity as its boundary. After cloning both hatch and circle entities, this method will restore these references in the cloned objects. When cloning multiple entities from a source to a target , only one clone context instance needs to be created, with the target model as parameter. See also the example below.

The cloning of an entity (or other object) may result in cloning a referenced entity indirectly. These are gathered in . The caller should add these indirectly cloned entities to the appropriate entity collection.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether duplicate names are allowed when cloning. The default value is false.
member.remarks: E.g. duplicate names are allowed, but the user may not intend this to happen.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CloneContext.RenameClashingBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to rename a block when a block with that name already exists in the target drawing. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When copying a user-defined block from one model to another and there is already a block with the same name, what is about to happen? If this property is true, the block is renamed and copied, if it is false than the block reference of the already existing block with the same name is taken.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CloneContext.CloneHeader
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to clone the header. Only relevant when cloning a whole model. The default value is false.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CloneContext.IndirectlyClonedObjects
member.summary: Gets the indirectly cloned objects that have not yet been added to the target model.
member.remarks: Some objects are cloned indirectly, e.g. a optionally has an associated annotiation (), which gets cloned too, but which is not added automatically to any target entity collection. The caller that makes the clones should add these indirectly cloned entities to the appropriate entity collection (this could be the model entities, layout entities or block entities).

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CloneContext.AddDefaultReactorToDictionaryEntries
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to add default a reactor to cloned dictionary entries. The default value is true.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether an exact copy has to be made (including handles etc). Only use this when copying a model exactly where the target model should be an identical copy of the source model.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Base.BlinnClipper.Fixed.Under
member.summary: Point is inside if real y is smaller than or equal to 1.
member.remarks: Intersection plane is defined by (0, -1, 0, 1). In Blinn terminology: boundary coordinate for point (x, y, z, w) is w - y.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Base.BlinnClipper.Fixed.Above
member.summary: Point is inside if real y is greater than or equal to 0.
member.remarks: Intersection plane is defined by (0, 1, 0, 0). In Blinn terminology: boundary coordinate for point (x, y, z, w) is y.

member.summary: Point is inside if real x is smaller than or equal to 1.
member.remarks: Intersection plane is defined by (-1, 0, 0, 1). In Blinn terminology: boundary coordinate for point (x, y, z, w) is w - position.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Base.BlinnClipper.Fixed.RightOf
member.summary: Point is inside if real x is greater than or equal to 0.
member.remarks: Intersection plane is defined by (1, 0, 0, 0). In Blinn terminology: boundary coordinate for point (x, y, z, w) is position.

member.summary: Point is inside if real z is greater than or equal to 0.

member.summary: Point is inside if real z is smaller than or equal to 1.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.ReferenceResolutionType
member.summary: How to handle missing referenced objects when cloning objects from one to another.
member.remarks:
E.g. a entity references a with name "X" that is not yet present in the target model where the entity is cloned to. In that case three options are available to resolve this:
Ignore the missing reference and use the default text style of the target model.
Clone the referenced text style.
Throw an exception when the text style is missing.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfTable2005
member.summary: Represents the obsolete AutoCAD 2005 table data structure. The table entity with which tabular data can be represented.

remarks.para: A table has an optional title row and an optional header row (for the column headers). Either one can be suppressed using the and flags. All subsequent rows are data rows. The title row, header row and data row cells have a instances from the associated with them, see , and .

The easiest way to setup a table is to create a DxfTable instance, and set the and . This will populate the and and create instances. Each cell can be accessed through the property. To change a cell's contents, set it's ValueFormat and Value.
The table entity was introduced in AutoCAD 2005.
Currently only by row/column cell styles are supported.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfModelerGeometry
member.summary: Represents a base class for all entities making use of the ACIS extension for AutoCAD.
member.remarks: The ACIS library was added to AutoCAD R13 for better support of 3D features like boolean geometry. The entities in the DXF/DWG file which represent ACIS data are just a thin wrapper around the internal textual format of ACIS, which is termed SAT. Each ACIS based entity is containing the content of a complete SAT file as encrypted text.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfHatch
member.summary: Represents a hatch pattern entity.

remarks.para: To define the hatch border, objects must be defined and added to .
There are two types of hatch filling: solid and pattern fill. To create a pattern fill hatch, set property . To create a solid fill hatch, set property to null (the default).
A pattern can be either created from code or by reading from a pattern file (see ).
The object coordinate system is defined by the and .
This entity was introduced in release 14.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfMText.Text
member.summary: Gets or sets the text value.
member.remarks:
This text may contain special processing sequences. Not all possible sequences are supported yet.
Supported processing sequences (note the the char after the backslash should be uppercase):
\ Use the backslash escape for the following characters: \{}~
\Cnnn;
Change color; nnn is the color number.
\P New line.
\FFONTNAME; Replace FONTNAME with the font name (e.g. romant.shx, Arial or Times New Roman). In case of shx fonts it's the font file name, in case of true type fonts it's the font name.
\U[+]nnnn;
DxfInsert a unicode character; nnnn is the unicode character number. If the plus sign is specified then nnnn is hexadecimal, otherwise decimal.
\Hffff;
Set new text height to ffff. Append an x to get a factor from the previous text height. So \H0.7x; reduces the text height to 70%.
{block} Curly braces indicate that the prefixed settings only apply to this block.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.DxfModel
member.summary: CAD model containing a CAD drawing ( objects, and tables).

remarks.para: A CAD model contains entities, which are either in model or paper space. When they are in model space, they are present in the model's collection. If they are in paper space, they are part of the DxfLayout.Entities of the (paper space) layout on which they are displayed.
Entities can be grouped in objects (see property DxfBlock.Entities), which can be referenced by zero or more entities.
Use / for reading into a CAD model object.
Use / for writing a CAD model object.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Actions.SimpleTransformationProviderBase
member.summary: A transformation provider which allows to define the provided transformations by a chain of simpler transformations.

remarks.para: The underlying idea is that the viewer is placed at the center of the coordinate system, and looking into -Z direction with X pointing right and Y pointing up (in DXF world coordinates, see ). So the first step is to place everything in a way that it is visible (i.e. the model is lying on the view axis in front of the viewer). This is done by the which is build from 3 (for 2D) or 4 (for 3D) simple transformations applied in the following order:
Project the model using either to project the model into screen space, or to project the model into a screen independent space where both X and Y are in the range -1 to 1.
The method is preparing all settings in a way that a model with a given bounding box is visible.

member.summary: Represents a line type that can be applied to a entity (property ).

remarks.para: A line type must have a .

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfTable
member.summary: The table entity with which tabular data can be represented.

remarks.para: By default when adding rows, the first row's gets assigned the , the second row gets assigned and subsequence rows get assigned the . The row/cell/cell content cell style instance may be changed, but must be present in .

The easiest way to setup a table is to create a DxfTable instance, and set the and . This will populate the and and create instances. Each cell can be accessed through the property. Too add content to a cell, create a instance and add it to . The contents collection also has Add overloads to facilitate adding contents.

The table entity has a containing the visual representation of the table data. Whenever a change is made to the table, method should be called to regenerate this block. When the block is not yet generated, it is generated automatically when the is written to file.
The table entity was introduced in AutoCAD 2005.

remarks.para: If a block is not present yet, an anonymous is created and added to the model to which the table belongs. If a block was already present it is cleared and refilled with new entities.

Call this method only if the table is part of a .

member.summary: Draws the horizontal lines, given the specified borders for all the columns of a row.

The top horizontal line of a double line is interrupted by connecting vertical double lines of the cells above (if they are there). The left and right coordinates are affected by whether the connecting vertical borders are double lines or not.

The bottom horizontal line of a double line is interrupted by connecting vertical double lines of the cells below (if they are there). The left and right coordinates are affected by whether the connecting vertical borders are double lines or not.
Draws single horizontal cell borders. The left and right coordinates are affected by whether the connecting vertical borders are double lines or not.

The left vertical line of a double line is interrupted by connecting horizontal double lines of the cells to the left (if they are there). The top and bottom coordinates are affected by whether the connecting horizontal borders are double lines or not.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Drawing.RenderedEntityInfo
member.summary: Represents a class containing information about a rendered entity.

remarks.para: A rendered entity info object contains information about an entity, together with the transformation matrix that was used to render the entity. This transformation can be used to transform back from the rendered coordinate system back to the entity's coordinate system (by using ). This is useful when manipulating an entity with the mouse.

A rendered entity may or may not have a . If it has a parent, it may have its own associated transformation matrix. Typically a chain is formed by inserts and a block's child entities, which may recurse a number of levels.

member.summary: Gets or sets the max repeat count of a line type when applied to an entity. In case the maximum is exceeded, the line type is not applied. The default value is 1000.
member.remarks: Sometimes an entity is very large compared to the total length of a line type pattern, potentially resulting in a single line being split into thousands of line segments. Use this setting to limit the amount of line segments produced for better performance.

member.summary: Gets or sets the max hatch pattern repeat count. The default value is 100,000.
member.remarks: Sometimes a hatch is very large compared to the hatch pattern. This property controls the maximum limit for the pattern repeat count. When this limit is exceeded, the hatch is drawing using a solid color.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Drawing.GraphicsConfig.PlotStyleManager
member.summary: Get or sets the plot style manager. The default is null, i.e. no manager.

member.summary: Base implementation.

remarks.para: This class serves as a base implementation. In its current form it doesn't do anything, but it's meant to be derived and used as a converter from entities to coordinates of line segment.

To get line segment coordinates of a or e.g. a the following must be done:
Create a object and pass a graphics factory as a parameter to its constructor.
Draw a using method or an using method . Pass the object as a parameter. The model/entity will draw itself on the graphics factory.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfViewport
member.summary: The viewport entity specifies a view in paper space on model space.

remarks.para: A viewport is part of a . The transformation from model space to paper space as specified by the viewport is only applied to entities in model space (see ). Model space entities are part of the model space layout, paper space entities are part of one of the paper space layouts. There may be be zero or more paper space layouts, there is only one model space layout (). Whether a layout is a model space or paper space layout is defined by property .
A viewport is by default in paper space.
The viewport with 1 represents paper space itself and does not show the model.

The defines the position at which the camera is looking in model space. The specifies the direction in which the camera is looking. The defines the view height in model space. The defines the view center in the display coordinate system (the model is transformed to the display coordinate system according to and and optionally the perspective transform). The specifies where the viewport is placed in paper space. Finally the defines the viewport size in paper space.

member.summary: Represents a class to draw 3D graphics onto a 2D plane using GDI .

remarks.para:
Usage:
Create intermediate drawable objects (points/lines/polylines) using .
Get bounding box using method .
Calculate the scale transform needed to fit the drawing into the display rectangle using . Set the result with the property.
Draw intermediate drawable objects using .
This intermediate representation is needed to speed up drawing when interacting with the graphics (e.g. rotating, panning, zooming).
2D rendering of and is supported, but not 3D. To disable drawing of image entities set property GraphicsConfig.DrawImages to false.

member.name: M:WW.Cad.Drawing.EntitySelector.GetClosestEntities(WW.Cad.Model.DxfModel,WW.Cad.Drawing.GraphicsConfig,WW.Math.Matrix4D,WW.Math.Point2D,WW.Cad.Drawing.EntityFilterDelegate,System.Double@)
member.summary: Gets the closest entities to specified 2D reference point.
member.param: The graphics configuration object determining aspects like precision.
The reference point to compare with.
The filter delegate to filter out entities to take into consideration (return true to include the entity). When null the default method is used.
member.returns: A list of rendered entities that meet the proximity criteria. Each rendered entity contains information about the entity, the transformation matrix that was used to render it and optionally has a parent. The parent is typically an insert, dimension or leader entity. Inserts may be nested multiple levels deep, thus leading to a parent chain.
member.remarks: Entities are first transformed by given transformation and transformed points are then compared to given 2D reference point. This method can e.g. be used to get the closest entity to the mouse position.

member.summary: Layer "containing" objects.

remarks.para: An entity is assigned to a layer by setting its Layer property. The layer must be part of the collection.
A layer can be enabled or disabled (see property ). When disabled the entities in that layer are not shown.

Similarly to this a layer can be frozen or thawed (see property ). Its function is almost identical to enabling/disabling, see a more elaborate AutoCAD manual for the differences (or e.g. ). Further more a layer can be frozen in a viewport by adding the layer to .

remarks.para: Attribute definition visibility is determined by property and DxfHeader.AttributeVisibility. When an attribute definition is part of a block, then the attribute definition is not displayed.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter
member.summary: This class will draw a CAD drawing onto a PDF document.

remarks.para: Add pages to the PDF document by calling one of the DrawPage overloads and call to close the document.
Note that the PDF x-axis points right and the y-axis points up, and the origin is at the bottom left.

The PDF exporter supports retaining text entities as text in PDF so the PDF can be searched for text and the text can be copied to the clipboard from the PDF file. To retain the text, set property GraphicsConfig.TryDrawingTextAsText to true. For some fonts and unicode characters this will not work properly, therefore the PDF exporter also supports font embedding. To enable font embedding set property to true (GraphicsConfig.TryDrawingTextAsText must be true as well). Font embedding does make the PDF file larger.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.LineWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the line width. The default value is 0.1.

remarks.para: Quote from the PDF spec: It is a nonnegative number expressed in user space units. A line width of 0 denotes the thinnest line that can be rendered at device resolution: 1 device pixel wide.

This value is only used if GraphicsConfig.DisplayLineWeight is set to false. Otherwise the normal line weight of the entity is used multiplied by GraphicsConfig.DotsPerInch, times the 100th of mm to inch factor. To choose a proper DotsPerInch value, take into account that the size of a PDF pixel is 1 / 72th of an inch.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.TextLineWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the line width for text entities. The default value is 0.1.

remarks.para: This value is only used if GraphicsConfig.DisplayLineWeight is set to false. Otherwise the normal line weight of the entity is used multiplied by GraphicsConfig.DotsPerInch, times the 100th of mm to inch factor. To choose a proper DotsPerInch value, take into account that the size of a PDF pixel is 1 / 72th of an inch.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.Body
member.summary: Gets the PDF body.
member.remarks: The document can be used to add further pages to the document, not using this exporter object. A PDF document can have 1 or more bodies. A single body represents a document revision. Since this exporter creates a new PDF document, there is just one body object.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.ModelSpaceLineWeightToPdfPixels
member.summary: Gets or sets the factor that is used to convert line weight to PDF pixels (used for model space only, not for paper space layouts).
member.remarks: The default value is 0.001 * , so line weight is translated to have the correct line width expressed in PDF pixels. Note that in model space the line weight is applied irrespective of the zoom factor or drawing units.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.UseMultipleLayers
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to use multiple layers. The default value is true.

remarks.para: By default the PDF exporter puts filled elements on the bottom layer, on top of this the stroked elements are put, and on the very top all text is drawn.
The PDF exporter has an alternative mode where elements are just drawn in the order in which they appear in the drawing.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.EmbedFonts
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to embed TrueType fonts in the PDF file. The default value is false. Set property GraphicsConfig.TryDrawingTextAsText to true for this property to take effect.

remarks.para: Please take care that embedding a font is only allowed if you have the proper license to embed the font.
This will only have an effect if text entities are converted as text.
PDF is notoriously bad displaying certain Unicode characters by default, so in order for them to appear correctly you may need to set this to true.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfDimension
member.summary: Represents an abstract dimension entity.

remarks.para: This is an abstract class, see the subclasses for the different types of dimensions.
To show feet/inches as linear dimension units, change the of the appropriate dimension style object.
The visualization of a dimension is handled by its which is generated by method upon writing a DXF file.

Take care that some of the definition points of the dimension are in object coordinate system (OCS), while others are in world coordinate system (WCS). OCS is defined by the value of the property, if it is not (0,0,1) then OCS ansd WCS differ by a rotation defined by or (the other way round) . Point properties defined in OCS have associated properties (ending with Wcs) which allow to set them in WCS. Furthermore the method allows to apply a different vector while taking care of updating OCS point properties accordingly.

member.example: An example of how to create a dxf file with an aligned dimension.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfDimension.ZAxis
member.summary: Gets or sets the extrusion direction.

remarks.para:
Setting this to something else than the default (0,0,1) means that all points of this dimension have to be transformed with the rotation transformation defined by
in order to get their world position. This is a relict of AutoCAD starting as a 2D CAD program.

So in order to set the definition points of this dimension correctly you'll have to transform the points with the inverse of this transformation (. Please note that the points of this entity are not updated automatically when setting this property, rather use the method when this dimension is already containing useful point date.
